doc.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Preparing mentally for a gig; writing ideas down
summary: Peterson avoids talking after 5 p.m. before a gig; both stress writing ideas down.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I have a thing I’ve had going for years and year now, when I’m on the road and I have to perform with the trio, even in nightclubs, after 5:00 at night, I don’t speak to anybody. Because mentally, I’m already thinking about that gig, you know? I’m thinking of all the things that I could do tonight that I maybe perhaps did not do last night or the night before, that I should correct and do properly, and it takes that kind of thought. And that’s what I tell them. I said, you know, “this is no fun and games thing, this is dedication.”
Many times my wife will say to me, “you didn’t hear what I said, did you?” And I say, “Darling, I’m sorry I didn’t hear you but I’m planning, I’m planning something, you

know, in our presentation, and consequently I didn’t hear you, so please forgive me, but you have my undivided attention now if you’ll repeat it.” You know but you have to plan it when it comes to you to do that.
When it happens. And you’d better, sometimes, write it down.
I’ve jumped up out of bed, halfway through the night with an idea for a tune. And—
About that composing that stuff, and writing, that’s good, no, it’s so good. You write it down.
I write it down or get it down on an instrument or record it or whatever, because the next day it might not come back, it might not come back.
